about.title: South San Francisco Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: When a fatal collision happens along US-101, Grand Avenue, or one of South San Francisco's other busy corridors, the family left behind faces grief alongside a maze of paperwork and legal deadlines. San Mateo County recorded 2 traffic deaths in the most recent full year of data, a reminder that behind every number is a household forever changed. California law gives a limited group of people, typically a spouse, domestic partner, or children, the right to bring a wrongful death claim, and dependents or other heirs may qualify in certain situations. There is a two-year window from the date of death to act, and that window shrinks significantly when a government entity is involved. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise results. We simply help South San Francisco families connect with an independent attorney who can walk through what happened, what the law allows, and what steps might make sense next.

whyChoose.title: What Families Should Understand About These Claims

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits standing to a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in specific circumstances. An attorney can clarify who in your family qualifies.

items.title: The Clock Starts Immediately
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file, but that period is much shorter if a government agency's road or vehicle was involved. Missing it can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows recovery for funeral costs and lost financial support, but also for the loss of love, companionship, and guidance a family member provided. These non-economic losses are part of the civil case, separate from any criminal proceeding.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim connected to a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a separate civil action, even if criminal charges are filed over the same crash. The two proceedings can move on different timelines and have different outcomes.

items.question: Does it matter that the crash happened on US-101 or a local road like Westborough Boulevard?
items.answer: Where the collision occurred can affect which agency owns or maintains the road, which matters for deadlines and evidence. An independent attorney reviewing the location can explain if a shorter government claim deadline applies.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free connection service, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. There's no obligation to move forward after the initial conversation.
